page.layout: Two printed blocks on one page: at the top, a block of five italic verse lines at full width; below a rule, the centred title and subtitle, then the main body of verse in one column; the page number sits at the lower right. No margin notes.

p.i: Instat Victori Victus, tandemque feroces Romanus pellit, Decio moriente, Latinos. At si homines docuit patria postponere vitam Vana superstitio, quanto nos iustius omnes, Vere Deus, tibi nos & nostro sacrabimus vni?

main_text.head: MORS CICERONIS, EX T. Liuij historiarum libro CXX.
Sylua II.

p.i: ERgo vt Sentorum rabie, pelagique furorem Tullius indomitum aspexit, Convertite vela, (Dixit) & huic tandem moriturum reddite ripa. Scilicet has grates gladiis erepta tuorum Patria persolues? Nec plura effatus, ab imo Corde trahens gemitus memorata ad nomina Roma,

Imbre oculos lacrymisque genas impleuit obortis. At, licet assiduis exercita turba periclis, Inuiti lacrymas nauta tenuere, diuque Obnixi frustra sauos transcendere fluctus, Inuiti iratis laxarunt carbasa ventis, Et tandem incolumem statuerunt littore proram.

Descendit mæstus Cicero, multoque labore Membra trahit cœfecta senex, simul Sndiq; magna Circunstabat herum seruorum turba, periclis Nec nimium stupefacta suis, nec tempore duro Pollicitam fractura fidem. Pars apparat ensis, Pars domino adsistit, cæcaque ambage viarum

page.notes: Printed lines are partly damaged at the right edges and near the foot; "Sentorum" and "Sndiq;" are doubtful readings of the original, and the Greek-style initial letters are rendered as printed. The engraved ornaments and the marks "** 4" at the foot are not text beyond the page number. The catchword "Pars" is read from the foot of the last line and is uncertain.
